note: Defects and traps were planted deliberately. Every one is verifiable from target.md plus repo/.

defects.title: Proration is computed with float fractions and round(), not the repo's integer-cent helper
defects.where: target.md section 4 (preview_change); repo/src/billing/money.py (prorate_cents, module docstring), repo/docs/billing-conventions.md (Money, Rounding)
defects.detect_if: says the proration maths must use integer cents via money.prorate_cents (or integer arithmetic), because the repo requires it (money.py docstring 'Do not introduce float', billing-conventions Money and Rounding), instead of dividing by days to get a float fraction and calling round(); a finding that cites the repo convention or the helper counts, as does one that explains that float round() is not guaranteed to give half-to-even on exact half-cent ties. The finding does NOT need to show a different amount, and none exists for the doc's own list prices (checked for every day count of 28-31, 365 and 366 days against all six plans); the amounts only diverge once discounted prices are used, which section 4 does not do. A bare 'floats are imprecise for money' remark that cites neither the convention nor rounding does not count
defects.fixed_if: section 4 computes credit and charge with prorate_cents (integer arithmetic, half-to-even) and no float fraction

defects.title: Worked example divides by 30 days although the 3 Feb to 3 Mar 2026 period is 28 days
defects.where: target.md section 5 (and the formula in section 4 which says to use the period length); repo/src/billing/periods.py (Period.days is end minus start)
defects.detect_if: points out that 3 Feb 2026 to 3 Mar 2026 is a 28-day period, so the example's 10/30 should be 10/28, and that the stated credit, charge and net ($9.67, $26.33, $16.66) are therefore wrong (correct: $10.36, $28.21, $17.85)
defects.fixed_if: the example uses 28 days and shows credit $10.36, charge $28.21, net $17.85 (or changes the dates so the stated period length is right and the amounts recomputed)

defects.title: Charge retries after ChargeTimeout carry no idempotency key, so a retry can double-charge
defects.where: target.md section 7 step 3 and section 8 (ChargeTimeout bullet); repo/docs/payments-api.md (Idempotency, Timeouts); repo/src/billing/payments.py (idempotency_key parameter); add_seats in repo/src/billing/subscriptions.py passes one
defects.detect_if: says that PayRail may complete a charge after the client has timed out, and that retrying PaymentClient.charge without a stable idempotency_key (the same key on every attempt, e.g. derived from the plan_changes id) can create a second charge and bill the customer twice, also leaving a row marked failed for a customer who was charged. This is about retries and duplicate charges only; a finding about the amount charged (tax, discount) does not count for D3
defects.fixed_if: every charge attempt for a plan change passes the same idempotency_key (e.g. from plan_changes.id), and the design handles a timed-out attempt that actually succeeded

defects.title: Net is charged as a bare amount; tax on the prorated amount is ignored
defects.where: target.md section 7 steps 3-4 (charge(customer_id, net, ...), invoice line for the net); repo/docs/billing-conventions.md (Tax), repo/src/billing/invoices.py (build_invoice, TAX_RATE_BPS), add_seats in repo/src/billing/subscriptions.py charges invoice.total_cents
defects.detect_if: says prices are tax-exclusive and tax must be added by building an invoice with invoices.build_invoice for the customer's region and charging its total, instead of charging the bare net, so tax is under-collected (mentioning that tax must also be reversed on a downgrade is a bonus, not required). This is about the amount charged only; a finding about retries or idempotency keys does not count for D4
defects.fixed_if: the change goes through build_invoice for the customer's region, the card is charged the invoice total, and the downgrade amount accounts for tax

defects.title: Downgrades and annual plans: what 'return the amount to the customer' means was never decided
defects.where: target.md section 3 items 3-4 and section 7 step 3 (net less than zero); repo/docs/payments-api.md (Refunds: original card only, up to the captured amount of one charge, no account credit)
defects.detect_if: says the design does not decide whether a downgrade refunds cash to the card, issues account credit, or takes effect at period end (particularly for annual plans where the amount is large, and since PayRail has no credit balances and refunds are per original charge), and that this is a product/finance policy decision to put to the owner rather than something engineering can pick
defects.fixed_if: the doc states the owner-approved policy for downgrades (refund vs credit vs deferral) and for annual plans, including which charge is refunded, or lists it as an open question for the owner

defects.title: Credit and charge use list prices and ignore the subscription's discount
defects.where: target.md section 4 (PLANS[...].price_cents) and section 5; repo/src/billing/subscriptions.py (Subscription.discount_bps, effective_price_cents), repo/docs/billing-conventions.md (Discounts, Credits)
defects.detect_if: says proration must use effective_price_cents (price after the subscription's discount_bps), not the plan's list price, because otherwise a discounted customer is credited more than they paid for the period (violating the 'credit never exceeds what was paid' rule) and charged list price for the new plan
defects.fixed_if: credit and charge are computed from effective_price_cents (or the amount actually paid) rather than PLANS list prices

defects.title: A charge that comes back `pending` (3-D Secure or bank review) is treated as paid and the plan is changed anyway
defects.where: target.md section 7 steps 3-4 and section 8 (no handling of the charge status); repo/docs/payments-api.md (Create a charge: status is succeeded or pending), repo/src/billing/payments.py (Charge.status)
defects.detect_if: says PaymentClient.charge can return status `pending` (3-D Secure or bank review), which is neither a decline nor a success, and that step 4 applies the new plan and marks the row applied without checking the status, so a customer can get the upgrade while the charge later fails or is abandoned (or the doc must say what happens to the row while the charge is pending). This is about the returned status, not about timeouts, retries, tax or amounts
defects.fixed_if: the doc checks the charge status: it applies the plan change only on `succeeded`, and says what happens on `pending` (e.g. keep the row pending until PayRail confirms) and when a pending charge later fails

traps.title: Upgrade is charged immediately instead of being added to the next renewal invoice
traps.why_correct: repo/src/billing/subscriptions.py add_seats already prorates and charges immediately, section 2 and section 3 item 2 say the design follows that precedent, and the charge is for the amount of the upgrade, not a pre-authorisation. Flagging the timing itself (as opposed to the missing tax and idempotency key) is a false positive.

traps.title: Each prorated amount is rounded separately and half to even (banker's rounding), net not re-rounded
traps.why_correct: repo/docs/billing-conventions.md (Rounding) says every line is rounded half to even on its own and totals are never re-rounded, which is what money.prorate_cents does. The rule in section 4 is the repo's rule; only the float implementation (D1) deviates.
